data.analysis: Keep N=3 and all role identities: the tracks test distinct direct-load, shared-memory, and register-reuse approaches. T1 and T3 share an X-coalescing hypothesis, but isolate one-output versus rolling-window reuse; T2 tests a different reuse mechanism. The critique found one correctness ambiguity worth clarifying: “period 63” must not be implemented as a naïve modulo-63 index or as an assumption that the stored endpoint planes are equal. The supplied baseline preserves in-range index 63 and wraps only out-of-range neighbor indices. Add that explicit guard to every objective. The baseline mean (3.5815 µs from three samples) motivates experiments but does not identify the bottleneck, so retain measurement as the arbiter.

revisions.objective: In src/candidate.cu, investigate a single direct-global-load kernel with one output per thread and no shared memory or per-thread multi-output reuse. Map each warp to adjacent X outputs at a fixed Y and Z, then compare suitable block/grid mappings and boundary-index handling. For each neighbor coordinate q=j+d, match the supplied boundary convention: add 63 if q<0, subtract 63 if q>63, otherwise leave q unchanged. Preserve in-range index 63; do not assume endpoint planes are equal. Compute all eight neighbors with the supplied coefficients and produce every output without modifying inputs or relying on scratch contents. Validate signed varying inputs, including independent endpoint values, against the oracle and compare repeated official full-run timings with the baseline.
revisions.subject: Coalesced direct-global one-output-per-thread kernel

revisions.objective: In src/candidate.cu, investigate a single shared-memory tiled kernel that loads Y neighborhoods cooperatively with contiguous X lanes and reuses the tile across multiple Y outputs. Explore tile heights and launch shapes while ensuring every required halo is initialized. Match the supplied boundary convention for each neighbor coordinate q=j+d: add 63 if q<0, subtract 63 if q>63, otherwise leave q unchanged; preserve in-range index 63 and do not assume endpoint planes are equal. Preserve the exact stencil, full output, input buffers, and scratch rules. Validate against the oracle on signed varying inputs, including independent endpoint values, then compare repeated official full-run timings with the baseline.
revisions.subject: Coalesced shared-memory Y tiles with explicit periodic halos

revisions.objective: In src/candidate.cu, investigate a single kernel where each thread handles several consecutive Y outputs using a register rolling window, with warp lanes still accessing adjacent X values. Explore small output-chunk sizes to balance neighbor reuse against register pressure and occupancy. Do not use shared memory or extra launches in this track. For each neighbor coordinate q=j+d, match the supplied boundary convention: add 63 if q<0, subtract 63 if q>63, otherwise leave q unchanged. Preserve in-range index 63; do not assume endpoint planes are equal. Compute every output for varying signed inputs and preserve the supplied tolerance and buffer constraints. Validate with the oracle and compare repeated official full-run timings with the baseline.
revisions.subject: Register rolling-window multi-output-per-thread kernel

data.shared_assumptions: All tracks hypothesize that mapping adjacent X values to warp lanes helps, but the 3.5815 µs three-sample baseline does not establish the bottleneck; measure the full official run. Preserve the supplied halo behavior per neighbor: q=j+d maps to q+63 when q<0, q-63 when q>63, and q otherwise. Thus index 63 remains in range; do not blindly use modulo 63 or assume endpoint planes match. Validate against the oracle with varying signed inputs, including independent endpoint values. Any later integration must be measured rather than assumed additive.
